# phux

> A terminal multiplexer whose server you can drive from code.

A background server owns terminals; clients and automation control them
through a public protocol, locally or across machines.

Start with the task guide below, not the complete architecture or decision archive.
Every documentation page has a direct .md URL, for example
https://docs.phux.sh/agents.md. You can also request any
page with `Accept: text/markdown`. Browsers get HTML by default.
[Every page in one file](https://docs.phux.sh/llms-full.txt): the whole
documentation as Markdown, in sidebar order, each page headed by its URL.

To find a topic, search the docs at
https://docs.phux.sh/search.json?q=your+query, which answers with the ten
best-matching sections as JSON, best first, each with its `url` (deep-linked
to the section's #anchor), the `markdown` of its page, its `page` and
`heading`, and a `text` snippet. Without `q` it answers with every section.
`q` is capped at 200 characters; CORS GET is allowed.

## Operating safely

Skills teach operation; they do not register tools or grant access to a server.
Use native phux_* tools with using-phux-tools when available, the local terminal
MCP adapter with using-phux-mcp, or the CLI with using-phux. Prefer a normal shell
tool for independent commands; use phux for persistent terminal state and
interactive programs. Check the installed version; phux --skill prints the
version-matched guide.

Discover exact pane selectors, read before writing, use finite observation
deadlines, and verify results. Do not type into the agent's own pane. A timeout
stops observation, not the process or already-sent input: inspect before retrying.
Ask before interrupting or destroying existing work.

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://phux.sh/install | sh         # phux CLI
curl -fsSL https://phux.sh/install-desktop | sh # macOS desktop app (+ CLI)
npx skills add no-phux/skills                    # agent skills
```

## Hosted services

- [Docs MCP server](https://phux.sh/mcp): streamable-HTTP, read-only. Tools:
  `search_docs`, `get_page` (any page as markdown), `get_install_command`,
  `latest_release`. It cannot see or control local terminals. Connect it with
  `claude mcp add --transport http phux-docs https://phux.sh/mcp` or
  `codex mcp add phux-docs --url https://phux.sh/mcp`.
  [Server card](https://phux.sh/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json).
- [Agent skills](https://phux.sh/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json):
  `using-phux`, `using-phux-mcp`, `using-phux-tools`.
- Live browser demo: `wss://shell.phux.sh/session` (anonymous edge shell, or
  authenticate with GitHub/Google for a native Linux shell).

## Documentation (docs.phux.sh)

- [Start here](https://docs.phux.sh/overview): guides and reference.
- [Install](https://docs.phux.sh/installation): supported platforms and installation channels.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.phux.sh/getting-started): start, split, detach, and inspect your first terminal.
- [Compare](https://docs.phux.sh/compare): phux, tmux, Herdr, and cmux.
- [Import tmux keys](https://docs.phux.sh/tmux-import): `phux config import-tmux` reads a running tmux and writes a preview.
- [Performance](https://docs.phux.sh/performance): measurements published with the comparison.
- [Use phux as an agent](https://docs.phux.sh/agent-quickstart): install phux and drive sessions from code.
- [Run coding agents](https://docs.phux.sh/agents): choose an integration and verify it works.
- [Know when Claude Code or Codex is waiting for you](https://docs.phux.sh/agent-waiting): `phux agent list` prints each pane's agent state; `blocked` means Claude Code, Codex, or another recognized agent is waiting on you.
- [Run a command in a pane and get its output and exit code](https://docs.phux.sh/pane-command): `phux run` types a command into a pane, waits, and exits with its status; includes a tmux mapping table.
- [Give your agent a terminal over MCP](https://docs.phux.sh/terminal-mcp): register `phux mcp`, the MCP server built into phux, so your agent can drive local panes.
- [ACP-owned sessions](https://docs.phux.sh/acp): provider readiness, typed commands, human permissions, and uncertain outcomes.
- [Remote access](https://docs.phux.sh/remote): connect machines and repair connections.
- [Reach your coding agents over Tailscale and SSH](https://docs.phux.sh/tailscale): list tailnet machines with `phux host discover`, or add one over SSH, then `phux attach`.
- [Clients](https://docs.phux.sh/clients): TUI, desktop, web, and native consumer paths.
- [Embed phux](https://docs.phux.sh/embedding): put a phux terminal in your own app with `phux-gpui`, `phux-client-runtime`, or `phux-client-ffi`. None is on crates.io yet.
- [Troubleshoot](https://docs.phux.sh/troubleshooting): diagnostics, persistence boundaries, and recovery.
- [Concepts](https://docs.phux.sh/concepts): running terminals, sessions, and shared control.
- [Automation reference](https://docs.phux.sh/scripting): selectors, input, waits, and structured results.
- [Build on phux](https://docs.phux.sh/building): the entry point for building on phux (CLI --json, MCP, watch, wire protocol, OSC 7501, plugins).
- [Any program can report status](https://docs.phux.sh/any-program-status): a program in a pane reports what it is doing with one OSC 7501 sequence, with no phux library, socket, or hook.
- [Command reference](https://docs.phux.sh/reference/cli): generated CLI documentation.
- [Server protocol](https://docs.phux.sh/protocol): how a client talks to a phux server in length-prefixed frames, with the handshake, capabilities, and the 1.x compatibility rule.
- [Architecture](https://docs.phux.sh/architecture): implementation and contributor reference.
- [A terminal multiplexer built on libghostty](https://docs.phux.sh/libghostty)
- [Historical decisions](https://github.com/no-phux/phux/tree/d21db2e345aeaff43a681b3a04dfd43f2cc082ca/docs/adr): immutable rationale archive, not current behavior. Live constraints and lookup commands are in Architecture.

## Programs and plugins

- [OSC 7501: report status from any program](https://docs.phux.sh/program-protocol): the Program Status Protocol sequence a program writes to report its status; phux records it and shows it per pane.
- [Program sequences and agent reports](https://docs.phux.sh/program-sequences): titles, `phux-ask` questions, OSC 133, OSC 52, and the other sequences phux reads, plus the agent record.
- [Plugin API](https://docs.phux.sh/plugins): a directory with a `phux-plugin.toml` manifest that adds actions, panes, sidebar sections, status-bar widgets, themes, hooks, and agent declarations.
